card.name: Start of next sentence in pregnancy risk text
card.fires_on: The word "All" opening the sentence that follows "background risk ... is unknown" in pregnancy risk statements. Also weaker on sentence-ending periods or linking words in label warnings.

modes.label: All pregnancies sentence
modes.description: The word All starting the standard sentence "All pregnancies have a background risk of birth defect" after an unknown-risk sentence.
modes.example: The estimated background risk of major birth defects and miscarriage for the indicated population(s) is unknown.<< All>> pregnancies have a background risk of birth defect

modes.label: Clause or sentence boundary in warnings
modes.description: A linking word or period in a warning sentence, right before the next statement begins.
modes.example: perforation of the stomach or intestines,<< which>> can be fatal.

card.writes: It seems to suppress continuations like Part or parte, and lightly favors words meaning afterwards or next time, so it pushes toward a new sentence.
card.plain: It fires at the point where one label sentence ends and the standard next sentence about pregnancy risk begins.
